play.analysis: {"analysis":"Daniil Medvedev's hard-court pedigree is the foundation here: he sits at 75% (15-5) over his last 20 hard-court matches, a decisively higher floor than Dalibor Svrcina's 53% (8-7) over his last 15 on the same surface. The head-to-head record favors Medvedev cleanly at 2-0, with the most recent meeting also played on hard court, which is precisely the surface we're on in Shanghai. Svrcina's recent form is uneven and venue-specific: he lost to Dimitrov on clay and to Tien on grass in first rounds, then beat lower-ranked opposition on hard courts (Darderi and Walton) before running into Shapovalov and losing in quarterfinals on a hard surface. Medvedev, despite a loss to Struff on grass in his most recent event, has a three-match winning streak on hard courts buried in that record (defeats of Merida Aguilar and Cilic, plus Atmane), which suggests he retains the technical foundation for this surface even if his grass-court block was choppy. The matchup shape favors Medvedev's consistency: Svrcina has not demonstrated the depth of hard-court reliability needed to threaten someone operating at a 75% clip on this exact surface, and the prior 2-0 head-to-head is concrete evidence of a real tactical or stylistic advantage rather than a statistical fluke.
